meta.title: First aid at road accidents
meta.pdd: Outside the text of the Rules: ERC 2025, RC UK 2025, the First Aid Rules and First Aid Standard of the Republic of Kazakhstan, ANZCOR, Highway Code UK, MedlinePlus; duty to help - para. 9(8) of the Rules; first aid kit - List of Defects, para. 38
meta.summary: You will learn how to make the scene of a road accident safe, who to call and what to say, how to recognise cardiac arrest and give cardiopulmonary resuscitation to an adult and a child, how to stop severe bleeding, what to do if you suspect a spinal injury, how to help a motorcyclist wearing a helmet, and what to do for burns, fractures and shock.

p: A driver involved in a road accident must stop, switch on the hazard warning lights, put out a warning triangle, take possible steps to give first aid to the injured, and call an ambulance. In an emergency the injured person is sent in a passing vehicle, and if that is not possible, taken to the nearest hospital in the driver's own vehicle ⟦10⟧.

First aid is not treatment. Your task is to keep the person alive until the medics arrive: call for help, prevent the person from dying of cardiac arrest or blood loss, and do no harm. Only do what you have been trained to do ⟦11⟧, and do not give the injured person anything to eat or drink (Highway Code UK, Annex 7).
The most common mistake is running out onto the carriageway to reach the casualty and becoming a second casualty yourself. A dead or injured rescuer helps no one.

Stop in a relatively safe place so that your vehicle does not obstruct traffic or create a new hazard. Switch on the hazard warning lights and put out the warning triangle: not closer than 15 m from the vehicle in a built-up area and 30 m outside it ⟦12⟧.
list: Assess the danger: the flow of traffic, smoke, fire, leaking fuel. The main dangers after a road accident are a further collision and fire (Highway Code UK, Annex 7)
Ask drivers to switch off their engines and do not let anyone smoke near the scene of the accident
Move anyone who is not injured away from the vehicles and off the carriageway to a safe place
If you have reflective or bright clothing, put it on (Highway Code UK, para. 283)
Before touching blood, put on medical gloves from the first aid kit or protect your hand with a plastic bag (American Red Cross)

p: Call an ambulance on 103, and other emergency services on 112 (First Aid Rules of the Republic of Kazakhstan, para. 16). Police - 102, fire and rescue service - 101. Connecting to the emergency services is free of charge (list of emergency services approved by the Government of the Republic of Kazakhstan).

Switch on the loudspeaker so that your hands stay free. The dispatcher may talk you through what to do, including how to give resuscitation ⟦13⟧. If the person does not respond, call at once and check breathing while the call is going through ⟦14⟧.
list: Where: the town, street and building, or the highway, kilometre marker, direction and landmarks
What happened: the road accident, how many vehicles, whether anyone is trapped in a vehicle, fire
How many casualties there are and what condition they are in: whether they are conscious, whether they are breathing, whether there is severe bleeding
Your phone number. Do not hang up first, until the dispatcher tells you to
lesson.tip: Give the location first: without an address, the crew will not find you.

p: Go up to the person and ask loudly: “Can you hear me?”, and gently shake their shoulders. If the person answers, do not move them unless necessary, ask what hurts, and watch them until the medics arrive.

If the person does not respond, call 112 or 103 on loudspeaker straight away and check breathing for no more than 10 seconds: look for chest movement, and listen and feel for breath ⟦15⟧. You should suspect cardiac arrest if the person does not respond and is not breathing normally. Occasional, gasping, “noisy” breaths are not normal breathing - they are a sign of cardiac arrest ⟦16⟧.
If the person does not respond and is not breathing normally, call 112 or 103 straight away and start chest compressions. Every minute without help reduces the chances of survival.
list: Lay the person on their back on a firm surface: resuscitation is more effective this way ⟦17⟧. If they are in a vehicle and not breathing normally, carefully remove them: saving a life matters more than the risk of a spinal injury
Place the heel of your hand on the lower half of the breastbone (the centre of the chest), your other hand on top, fingers interlocked, arms straight
Compression depth: 5-6 cm, rate: 100-120 per minute
After each compression, let the chest fully recoil, and do not lean on it. Keep interruptions in compressions as short as possible

If you are trained: 30 compressions, then 2 rescue breaths (about a second each, enough to make the chest visibly rise). If you are not trained or not willing to give rescue breaths, give continuous compressions only
If there is an automated external defibrillator (AED) nearby, have someone bring it: anyone can use it - switch it on and follow its voice prompts
If there are two of you, swap roles roughly every 2 minutes and make the changeover quick (AHA 2025)
Continue until the medics take over, until the person wakes up and starts breathing normally, or until you no longer have the strength ⟦18⟧
lesson.tip: Numbers for the exam and for life: 5-6 cm, 100-120 per minute, 30:2.

p: If consciousness is impaired because of illness, the person is breathing normally and there are no signs of injury (for example, they felt unwell rather than being hurt in the accident), turn them into the recovery position. This stops the tongue or vomit from blocking the airway ⟦19⟧.

With agonal breathing, and with an injury, for example after a road accident, do not put the person into the recovery position ⟦20⟧. Only turn them onto their side if they start to vomit or have trouble breathing (see the next section).
Keep checking their breathing constantly. If it becomes abnormal or stops, turn them onto their back again and start resuscitation.
Neck and back injuries are common after a road accident. That is why a casualty is not pulled out of a vehicle or moved unless necessary (Highway Code UK, para. 283).
You may move the person only if they are in immediate danger (fire, risk of a further collision) or if resuscitation cannot otherwise be carried out.

If the person is conscious, ask them not to move and to hold their head in a comfortable, stable position. Never force them into a different position. If an unconscious person is lying on their back, kneel at their head and hold their head and neck in a neutral position with your hands ⟦21⟧. Do not fit a cervical collar unless you have special training.

Breathing matters most: opening the airway is more important than keeping the neck still ⟦22⟧. If such a casualty starts to vomit or has trouble breathing, carefully turn them onto their side, keeping the head, neck and torso in line, preferably with two people.
lesson.tip: Rule for road accidents: do not move the person unless there is a direct threat to life.

p: With severe bleeding, a person can die within minutes, so act at once.
list: Press firmly and continuously on the wound with your hand through clean cloth or a dressing. This is the main method ⟦23⟧
If the dressing becomes soaked through, do not remove it - put another one on top and keep pressing (American Red Cross)
If an object is sticking out of the wound, do not remove it: pad around it with rolls of cloth and press around it (Highway Code UK, Annex 7)

If bleeding from an arm or leg is life-threatening and direct pressure does not help, apply a tourniquet. A tourniquet is included in the first aid kit (Ministry of Health of the Republic of Kazakhstan)
Apply the tourniquet 5-7 cm above the wound, not over a joint. Tighten it until the bleeding stops ⟦24⟧
Write down the time you applied the tourniquet and be sure to tell the medics ⟦25⟧
Do not loosen or remove the tourniquet yourself: only medics should do this ⟦26⟧

p: Cool the burn with cool running water as soon as possible: ANZCOR and Highway Code UK recommend at least 20 minutes, the First Aid Standard of the Republic of Kazakhstan at least 15 minutes. Cooling can help even if started within 3 hours of the burn, but the sooner the better (ANZCOR 9.1.3).

Do not use ice, snow or icy water, do not apply oil, cream or ointment, and do not burst blisters. Remove rings and watches near the burn, but do not pull off anything stuck to the skin. Then loosely cover the burn with a clean non-stick material or cling film and keep the person warm so they do not become too cold (ANZCOR 9.1.3).

If someone's clothing is on fire, do not let them run: lay them down, cover them with heavy cloth and roll them over. Battery acid is rinsed off with running water for at least 20 minutes (ANZCOR 9.1.3).

If you suspect a fracture, do not try to straighten the limb or set the bone, and do not check whether it moves. Immobilise it in the position you found it in, supporting the areas above and below the injury. If a bone is visible in the wound, cover the wound with a clean dressing and do not touch the bone (First Aid Standard of the Republic of Kazakhstan, para. 8; MedlinePlus).
Shock is a dangerous condition after a severe injury or blood loss. Signs: pale, cold, clammy skin, a fast weak pulse, shallow breathing, restlessness or confusion (MedlinePlus).
list: Stop any bleeding

Lay the person on their back. Raise the legs about 30 cm, but only if there is no injury to the head, neck, back or legs and it does not cause pain (MedlinePlus). Such injuries are often possible after a road accident, so the legs are usually not raised
Cover them to keep them warm
Do not give them anything to eat or drink: this can cause vomiting and choking (MedlinePlus, Highway Code UK)
If the person vomits, turn them onto their side - if a spinal injury is suspected, turn them “as one unit”, without twisting (MedlinePlus)

p: If you have not been trained in child resuscitation, act as you would with an adult: check for a response, call an ambulance straight away and follow the dispatcher's instructions ⟦27⟧.

Resuscitation of a child begins with 5 initial rescue breaths. After that, rescuers trained in child resuscitation alternate 15 compressions with 2 breaths; everyone else uses 30 and 2 ⟦28⟧. The First Aid Standard of the Republic of Kazakhstan gives 30:2 for children. Compress the chest by at least a third of its depth, but no deeper than 6 cm, at 100-120 times a minute (RC UK 2025; under the Standard of the Republic of Kazakhstan, for children aged 1-12, 4-5 cm). If you are alone and have no phone, give resuscitation for 1 minute first, then go for help. A defibrillator may be used on children: for children under 25 kg (roughly up to age 8), switch to the paediatric mode if the device has one.
Do not remove a helmet from an injured motorcyclist unless it is necessary to save their life: removing it can easily injure the neck (Highway Code UK, para. 283).

If the person is not breathing normally and the helmet is preventing you from opening the airway and starting resuscitation, remove the helmet: the airway matters more than keeping the neck still ⟦29⟧. If possible, do this with two people: one holds the head and neck, while the other carefully slides the helmet off without twisting it.

lesson.h: The first aid kit, and if someone is choking
p: Under the List of Defects, a car, truck, bus or wheeled tractor may not be used without a first aid kit, a fire extinguisher and a warning triangle, and a motorcycle with a sidecar may not be used without a first aid kit and a warning triangle ⟦30⟧. The Ministry of Health of the Republic of Kazakhstan sets the contents of the first aid kit (Order No. 118/2020): it contains a tourniquet, bandages, a dressing pack, plasters, gloves, scissors, a resuscitation face shield, a survival blanket and antiseptic wipes, but no medicines.

If someone is choking and coughing, encourage them to keep coughing. If the cough stops or becomes ineffective, give up to five back blows, then, if needed, up to five abdominal thrusts, and call an ambulance. Do not sweep the throat blindly with your fingers. If they lose consciousness, start resuscitation ⟦31⟧.

keyFacts: A driver involved in a road accident must give first aid and call an ambulance ⟦1⟧
Put out the warning triangle not closer than 15 m in a built-up area and 30 m outside it ⟦2⟧
Ambulance - 103, other emergency services - 112, police - 102, fire and rescue - 101; the call is free (First Aid Rules of the Republic of Kazakhstan, para. 16; list of emergency services)
Not responding and not breathing normally is a sign of cardiac arrest; gasping breaths do not count as breathing ⟦3⟧
Compressions for an adult: depth 5-6 cm, rate 100-120 per minute ⟦4⟧
A trained rescuer gives 30 compressions and 2 breaths; an untrained one gives continuous compressions only ⟦5⟧
Recovery position - if consciousness is impaired by illness, breathing is normal and there is no injury; do not use it if there is an injury ⟦6⟧
If a spinal injury is suspected, do not move the person unless there is immediate danger ⟦7⟧
Tourniquet - only for life-threatening bleeding from a limb, 5-7 cm above the wound, not over a joint, with the time recorded ⟦8⟧
Cool a burn with cool running water for at least 20 minutes, without ice; the Standard of the Republic of Kazakhstan requires at least 15 minutes (ANZCOR 9.1.3, Highway Code UK)
Do not straighten a fracture; immobilise it in the position found (First Aid Standard of the Republic of Kazakhstan, para. 8; MedlinePlus)
In shock, lay the person down, keep them covered, and do not give them anything to eat or drink (MedlinePlus, Highway Code UK)
mistakes: “Run to the casualty first.” Safety comes first: hazard warning lights, the warning triangle, assessing the danger. Otherwise there will be more casualties.
“If the person is wheezing and taking occasional breaths, they must be breathing.” Infrequent gasping breaths are a sign of cardiac arrest, and you need to start resuscitation ⟦9⟧.

“You must pull the casualty out of the vehicle straight away.” If a spinal injury is suspected, do not move the person unless there is a direct danger (for example, fire) or resuscitation is needed (Highway Code UK, para. 283).
“You should put oil on a burn or apply ice.” What is needed is cool running water for at least 20 minutes, without ice, oils or creams (ANZCOR 9.1.3).
“A broken arm must be straightened.” Do not straighten the limb; immobilise it in the position you found it in.
“Give water to a casualty in shock.” They must not eat or drink: this can cause vomiting and choking (MedlinePlus).
